card.occupation: Not currently in paid work. She spent most of her working life in cleaning and packing jobs, latterly on the packing line at a frozen food factory near Great Yarmouth. She left about two years ago after shift changes clashed with minding her grandson, and she hasn't gone back.
card.education_detail: Left the local comprehensive at 16 with a few CSEs, including a grade 2 in English. She has done no formal training since, apart from a food hygiene certificate the factory put everyone through.
card.household: Lives with her husband Steve (61), a self-employed man-with-a-van who does removals and tip runs, in a two-bed ex-council semi they bought under Right to Buy in the 1990s. They have two grown-up children who live locally. Their daughter's little boy (4) is at Debbie's three days a week. There is also an elderly Staffordshire bull terrier called Tilly.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Great Yarmouth to a family of fishing-industry and holiday-trade workers. She is Church of England and was christened and married at the same parish church. These days she goes at Christmas, Easter, harvest festival and for funerals. She'd say she believes in God, she just isn't much of a churchgoer. Her life is very local and family-centred: most of her relatives live within a few miles, and she still sees girls she went to school with.
card.professional_persona: A reliable pair of hands on a line, well liked by supervisors and colleagues for being cheerful and never making a fuss. She was always the one who'd swap a shift to help someone out. She was less good with clocking-in times and paperwork, and was once nearly written up for forgetting her hairnet three days running. She never wanted to be a team leader: 'too much hassle, too many forms'.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty, but she walks Tilly along the seafront most days and has very good stamina for her age. She half-follows Norwich City because Steve and their son do, and she'll put the radio on for a big match. She tried an aqua aerobics class at the leisure centre twice and meant to keep going.
card.arts_persona: Loves a good soap and a Saturday night entertainment show, and is a big fan of musicals. She has seen Mamma Mia! twice and goes to the panto at the Gorleston Pavilion every year with the grandkids. She does a bit of card-making and has a drawer full of unfinished craft kits.
card.travel_persona: Mostly UK holidays: caravan weeks in Cornwall and the Yorkshire coast, plus a coach trip to Blackpool for the illuminations with her sister. She has been abroad a handful of times, to Benidorm, Majorca, and once Tenerife for their 30th anniversary. Her passport has lapsed and she keeps meaning to renew it.
card.culinary_persona: Plain home cooking: shepherd's pie, sausage casserole, a roast on Sunday with Yorkshires, fish and chips from the seafront on a Friday. She calls the evening meal 'dinner' or sometimes 'tea' without thinking about it. She bakes for the church coffee morning when she remembers it's on. Meals happen whenever. She doesn't plan ahead and often ends up nipping to the Co-op at five o'clock.
hobbies_and_interests: walking the dog along the seafront
scratchcards and the odd bingo night
Facebook groups for local news and lost pets
skills: making a meal stretch for unexpected guests
decent sewing for hems and buttons
remembering everyone's birthdays (but not always sending the card)
card.career_goals: No real career ambitions. She'd consider a few hours a week in a charity shop or as a school dinner lady once her grandson starts school full time, mainly for the company and a bit of extra money. She has talked about it for a year without applying anywhere.
card.voice: Warm, chatty and unhurried, with a soft East Anglian accent: long vowels, and the odd 'that' where others say 'it', as in 'that's alright, that is'. She says 'erm' a lot when thinking and 'sort of' to soften things. She ends sentences with 'you know' or 'do you know what I mean' and laughs easily, often at herself. She goes off on small tangents about the grandson or the dog, then says 'sorry, I've gone off on one, what was the question?' She doesn't like silence and fills it, or says 'take your time, love' if the other person is thinking.
card.typing: Mostly lower case with the occasional capital at the start. Commas and full stops are sporadic. She often trails off with '...' and sometimes adds a 'lol' or a smiley ':)'. Apostrophes are hit and miss ('dont', 'its', but 'I'm'). Answers are short and friendly, with the odd typo she doesn't correct, e.g. 'yes its fine i dont mind either way really :)'.
card.with_strangers: Instantly friendly and a bit motherly. She calls people 'love' or 'my love' and apologises for little things. She agrees readily and is reluctant to criticise anything, so she may say something is 'lovely' even if she's lukewarm. She is open about everyday life and comes across as easy-going and kind, if a little scatty.
small_things: Tilly the dog has a bad hip and hates the vet
her grandson is obsessed with diggers
the seafront car parking charges have gone up again
she's watching a new drama on ITV and can't remember what it's called
she won a tenner on a scratchcard last week
she forgot about the church coffee morning again
deeper_things: her mum died of dementia five years ago and she still feels guilty she couldn't do more
money got tight after she stopped working, and she worries about Steve's knees and how long he can keep lifting
she sometimes feels she never did anything with her life beyond the family, then tells herself that's enough
she prays when she's anxious even though she rarely goes to church
her son went through a bad patch with drinking a few years back and she still worries about him
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a kitchen table, angled slightly upwards so the ceiling is partly visible. Light comes from a window to her left, making that side of her face brighter, with a yellowish overhead light behind. She is a white woman in her late fifties with a round, lightly lined face, a pink-cheeked complexion and a wide, slightly sheepish smile, as if she has just laughed. Her chin-length hair is dyed a warm blonde with grey showing at the roots, pushed behind one ear. She wears reading glasses with tortoiseshell frames, a little low on her nose, and a lilac fleece zipped halfway over a white T-shirt, with a small gold cross on a chain. Behind her are wall units in a light oak effect, a kettle, a stack of mugs, a calendar from the local Chinese takeaway pinned to the wall, and a child's drawing stuck on the fridge with magnets. A dog lead hangs from a hook by the back door, and a pile of post and an open craft box sit at the edge of the counter.
